mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays depressed while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, weekday foot traffic and discretionary shopping will keep weakening, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is -32.0 and TRANSIT is -55.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 28-day mean even though WORKPLACES stays below -20 and TRANSIT stays below -45 for the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above its recent level signals more time spent at home, which reduces in-person discretionary shopping and drives RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stays positive at 12.7 in t-0w after 14.1 in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 10 for most of that period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls further below its already severe trough, the city is likely in a tightening or compliance shock that suppresses mall and street retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60 on a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -55.9 at t-0w and was -56.4 in t-1w/t-2w
failure_condition: A weekly TRANSIT reading below -60 is followed by stable or rising RETAIL_REC over the subsequent 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a prior holiday or weather dip should precede stronger leisure activity and spill over into retail-and-recreation spending, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -5.3 at t-3w to 21.6 at t-2w before easing to -8.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: A week-on-week PARKS increase above 10 points is not followed by a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain elevated, households are substituting toward local, necessity-based trips and away from leisure shopping, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is positive at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days despite both GROCERY_PHARM staying above 0 and RESIDENTIAL staying above 10.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rebound in PARKS after weeks of subdued outdoor movement can produce a delayed leisure and shopping spillover, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -8.9 at t-0w to 3.4 at t-1w and 21.6 at t-2w
failure_condition: A positive turn in PARKS is not followed by any increase in RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together from current lows, retail-and-recreation mobility should improve as commuting, errands, and after-work trips return, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series remain far below baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 28-day mean over the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in GROCERY_PHARM from its current mild positive level would indicate fading holiday or stock-up behavior, and that same cooldown should spill into lower discretionary retail mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM drops below 0 after being positive
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is 1.9 at t-0w after 6.6 and 4.9 in prior weeks
